newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs end sharply higher as stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs end sharply higher as stocks fall.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher on Thursday.
A nosedive in Tokyo share prices was partly responsible for the jump in JGBs, traders said.
The market now sees falls in Tokyo share prices as a positive factor for JGBs, a city bank trader said.

"Before, the market felt that weak share prices may lead to profit-taking sales of JGBs... But now traders feel that a fall in share prices will lead to a continuation of the Bank of Japan's low-interest rate policy, which is encouraging buying of JGBs," the trader said.
In the Tokyo stock market, the benchmark Nikkei 225 tumbled 522.36 points, the third largest one-day drop this year, or 2.60 percent to settle at 19,570.67.
The March ended at 125.92, up from Wednesday's 125.46.
Investors were detected buying cash JGBs during the day, traders said.
A trader for a city bank's securities affiliate said investors such as life insurers were detected buying cash JGBs with around three-year maturities.
"Some investors were apparently eager to buy JGBs before the end of the year," the trader said.
The first trader said investors were said to have bought long-term cash JGBs.
It will be interesting to see what investors decide to do in light of weak Tokyo share prices, the second trader said.

"Will they decide to take no action, or will they choose to sell JGBs to take profits as some had thought they would do? It will probably take two or three days to get an idea of what their chosen course of action will be," the trader said.

Market participants had expected the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to conduct outright JGB purchases this morning, but its bond purchase operation at 10.10 a.m. (0110 GMT) was through repurchase agreements, not outright.
The negative impact on the market was limited, traders said.

"The BOJ needed to roll over the expiring repo agreements today, but the bank does not conduct repo and outright operations on the same day. Hence, probably for that reason, the BOJ refrained from doing an outright purchase operation today," said a trader for another city bank's securities unit.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.385 percent as of 0704 GMT, down from previous day's 2.425 percent.
